messages.subject: [NMF-user] setting the fraction of genes randomly sampled in an iteration?
messages.subject_clean: [NMF-user] setting the fraction of genes randomly sampled in an iteration?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

no, all genes/features are included in each run. What changes is the seed,
i.e. starting point, which is different and randomly generated at each run.

Standard consensus clustering analysis would use a different set of
_samples_ for each run. This is fine for evaluating the accuracy/stability
of classification, but makes it difficult to link features to sample
groups, since each run (vote) returns a somehow different set of
component-specific feature: what set of features or basis components should
be used? average? consensus?
Would be nice to incorporate a function/option to  easily perform such
analysis though.

There is still some methodology to be developed around this point. A
technical issue also arise in term of memory/speed, if one wants to compute
complete feature consensus matrices.
I am happy to hear/discuss on this.
My time is currently very limited, although bringing the package back to
CRAN is quite high on my todo list.

Renaud

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to install NMFged and CellMix in R-2.15.3, but it seems that
for both versions there are problems with the current (v0.10.3) package
of NMF. I managed to finally install the current NMF version after
fixing some incompatibilities with the current pkgmaker package from rforge, but did
not succeed to get either of the two target packages up and working.
There seem to be incompatibilities between NMF v0.10.3 and NMFged, and
some other problems with pkgmaker/registry for CellMix.

I found a vignette of NMFged that says that it requires NMF v0.5.99, but
I am unable to find that package version anywhere.

I guess that CellMix is still under development.  However, is there a
way to get the NMF version (v0.5.99) required to get at least NMFged
running ? I'm on Ubuntu 12.04, if that matters. If you want I can send
more detailed error descriptions, but for now I probably would be fine
with the old NMF version.

Thanks a lot and best regards,
Hilmar

On 2013-03-18, at 12:55 AM, Renaud Gaujoux wrote:

Hi,

no, all genes/features are included in each run. What changes is the seed, i.e. starting point, which is different and randomly generated at each run.

Standard consensus clustering analysis would use a different set of _samples_ for each run. This is fine for evaluating the accuracy/stability of classification, but makes it difficult to link features to sample groups, since each run (vote) returns a somehow different set of component-specific feature: what set of features or basis components should be used? average? consensus?
Would be nice to incorporate a function/option to  easily perform such analysis though.

There is still some methodology to be developed around this point. A technical issue also arise in term of memory/speed, if one wants to compute complete feature consensus matrices.
I am happy to hear/discuss on this.
My time is currently very limited, although bringing the package back to CRAN is quite high on my todo list.

Renaud
